fields.v: - Course SDD conventions + agents chosen freely (Claude Code 10 projects, Codex 5, Antigravity/Gemini 5, GitHub Copilot 3, also OpenCode, DeepSeek, ChatGPT; 7 teams used more than one) + models Not stated per project (trailer example claude-code/claude-sonnet-5-5): criterion: the assignment's requirements (public URL, >= 100,000 lines, dated spec written before the code, every prompt recorded) and conventions; no success criterion for SDD itself stated by the authors; no per-agent breakdown. Results: URL 17/18; spec first 53-90% (15 projects); 3 projects recorded no session, sessions cover 48% of agent commits; trailers median 69%; specs mostly agent-written (69%), only 39% of lines traced to a spec, 14% of specs added with code; 3 teams reached 100k lines only with unused generated code, 1 team backdated specs by rewriting history. Quality verdict: partly against the assignment requirements (met unevenly); no criterion stated by the authors for whether SDD kept students in control. Cost verdict: not measured
fields.quote: It had four requirements: the application had to open at a public URL; it had to have at least 100,000 lines of code, counted with cloc excluding dependencies, lock files, build artifacts, documentation, and data; each part of the system needed a dated specification in a SPEC/ folder, written before the code it describes
fields.why: The verdict 'does not work' rests on the extractor's reading ('specs did not keep students in control'); the only criteria the authors state are the assignment requirements, which were met partly (e.g. URL 17/18, spec first 53-90%), so the verdict should follow those or be 'no criterion stated by the authors'.
fields.doubt: O veredicto 'não funciona' parece ser juízo teu: os autores só dão como critério os requisitos do trabalho (URL, 100k linhas, spec antes do código, sessões gravadas), cumpridos em parte. Lê a pág. 2 (§II.A) e a pág. 5 (RQ1) e decide entre 'parcialmente' face a esses requisitos ou 'sem critério declarado pelos autores'.

fields.v: Self-reported: hours dedicated (median 8), share of generated code read before committing (median 30%); share of ideas (median 50%) and code (median 20%) attributed to self; recorded prompts (741 prompts, median 15 words per prompt; 13% at most three words)
fields.quote: In the sessions we could parse, students wrote 741 prompts, with a median of 15 words; 13% have at most three words, such as “continue”.
fields.where: §IV.A RQ1: Do students follow the rules of the assignment?, p. 5
fields.why: The 15-word median is the length of each prompt, not a count of prompts per session as the field says.
fields.doubt: O campo diz 'prompts por sessão', mas o artigo dá 741 prompts com mediana de 15 palavras por prompt (comprimento, não número por sessão). Confirma na pág. 5 e corrige a descrição da métrica.
